memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Your male and female slaves are to come from the nations around you; from
them you may buy slaves. You may also buy some of the temporary residents
living among you and members of their clans born in your country, and they
will become your property'" - Lev 25:44-45 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard passage for modern readers, and we should not pretend
otherwise. God permitted Israel to acquire bondservants from surrounding
nations under different terms than those governing their fellow Israelites.
We must handle this honestly rather than smoothing it over.

A few things help us read it rightly. First, this was regulation within the
harsh realities of the ancient world, not God's ideal for humanity. From the
beginning, all people are made equally in God's image (Gen 1:27), and
Scripture consistently condemns the man-stealing that fuelled later slave
trades (Exod 21:16; 1 Tim 1:10). Second, even here God places these people
under law and protection, not outside it.

Third, and most importantly, we read the Old Testament in the light of where
Scripture is heading. The whole trajectory of the Bible moves toward
liberation and the equal dignity of every person. Paul declares that in
Christ there is neither slave nor free, for all are one in Him (Gal 3:28). He
tells Philemon to receive his servant as a beloved brother (Philem 16). The
gospel planted the seed that would one day dismantle slavery itself.

Dear reader, we do not need to defend every ancient institution to trust
God. We follow a Saviour who came to set captives free (Luke 4:18), and whose
gospel dignifies every human being. Let that trajectory shape how you value
every person you meet.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I hold on to the truth that every person bears God's image equally?
2. How does the gospel's direction toward freedom shape my view of others?
3. Where might I need to honour the dignity of someone the world overlooks?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your gospel moves toward freedom and dignity for all.
Give me Christ's heart for every person, and help me honour Your image in
everyone I meet. Amen.
